meta.title: Bully Pulpit International: the growth plan
meta.subject: Bully Pulpit International (BPI), a BSP portfolio company since 2023-04-27
meta.thesis: From agency to productized communications company: AI-era reputation work, public affairs for regulated sectors (energy, AI, health), European add-ons and retainers over projects. Add-ons are specialist shops; AI agents handle monitoring, compliant drafting and audience testing.
meta.method: Built on 2026-10-06 from the repo sources BPI filings (estimate table, FEC/Companies House/Form D items), BSP firm profile (bsp-bpi add-ons, timeline, BPI opportunities), public comparables (communications agencies benchmarks), PE landscape (sponsors overlapping BPI), ServiceOS evidence (ra-bpi, kb-bpi-*, ve-20..23, vs-bpi-*) and rival filings (FGS, Precision Strategies, Stagwell). Added web research fetched 2026-10-06: BSP Smith + Howard exit release, Canaccord/O'Dwyer's/PrivSource for Penta, Wikipedia/WPP 6-K for FGS, CVC for Teneo, BPI releases, Forrester TEI pages (Writer, Quid, Microsoft), EY/Aaru, Muck Rack via GlobeNewswire, Quorum, Davis+Gilbert 2025 PDF (text-extracted) and the IPA Agency Census 2025. Expansion-phase data points are computed in code from the repo sources (cadences, ratios, sums of opportunity ceilings). KPI targets and KPI roadmap are explicit analyst assumptions anchored to the BPI filings midpoints.
caveats: BPI revenue, EBITDA, headcount and debt are low-confidence analyst estimates from BPI filings, not company disclosures. Every KPI target and KPI roadmap figure is an assumption (label est.).

FEC figures are gross political billings, mostly pass-through media, not BPI revenue. The 2022 figure ($3.1M) comes from the BPI filings financial picture because the item-level cycle series was removed in verification.

Penta revenue ($100M+, about half from AI/data) is per Axios (Aug 2025), captured from a search-result extract. Axios returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch, and the O'Dwyer's and Canaccord pages confirm the deal but not revenue.
Teneo ~$700M valuation comes from press summaries (PRovoke/Holmes Report via search). The CVC release confirms 800+ staff, 19 offices and 9 acquisitions since 2015 but not the price.

AI-agent metrics are vendor-commissioned (Forrester TEI for Writer, Quid, Microsoft) or vendor case studies (Aaru/EY, Quorum). They are self-selected upper bounds. The Writer study also shows clients cutting agency scope by 50%, a substitution risk for BPI.

Federal opportunity total ($250M) sums ceilings/values as parsed from BPI opportunities and is dominated by the NASA recompete ($202.6M base plus all options). Eligibility and set-aside status are unverified.
International revenue share (~15-20% today) is an analyst estimate from UK Companies House staff counts and an assumed GBP/USD of 1.27. Germany and Nordics revenue is not public.

pp_nationwide.json (the named structural template) was not present in the repo at build time, so field conventions follow assets/chat.js expansionPlan(). talent program replaces pro program and phases carry KPI targets with headcount/locations instead of technicians/territories.
Smith + Howard and BPI add-on cadences are computed from first-close/announcement dates and count Seven Hills and Message House as two add-ons.
meta.narrative: Six add-ons since April 2023 (about 2.0 a year versus Smith + Howard's 2.4) show BPI already running the Smith + Howard plan across the Atlantic, with London its #2 hub and Germany its #3 market. Smith + Howard grew from about 100 people in one Atlanta office to about 800 in 11 locations, with 9 add-ons and nearly 4x revenue, then sold to TPG Growth in August 2026. BPI's version starts from a larger base: an estimated $85-125M of net revenue, roughly $17-28M of adjusted EBITDA and about 400 people; those are low-confidence estimates from filings, not company figures. The biggest value gap is cyclicality; federal political billings swung from $3.1M in 2022 to $115.3M in 2024, and Stagwell's comparable segment fell 16.5% organically in the year after the election. So phase one productizes the core; SignalOS packages narrative monitoring, synthetic message testing and outcome dashboards into always-on retainers, sold first through the 2026 Reputation Resilience Index briefings, where 81% of adults say AI makes false rumors too easy to spread. Phase two builds named practices where regulation guarantees recurring work (AI and tech policy, energy and critical minerals, health in Boston, and litigation and oversight), plus a federal capture team for about $250M of tracked agency communications recompetes where BPI has no prime awards today. Phase three is the transatlantic version of regional-to-national; one retainer should cover Washington, Brussels, Berlin and London, built with 2-3 specialist tuck-ins a year funded under the existing PineBridge facility, whose UK collateral package is already in place. The analogs show the exit path; Penta was built from a data asset, added Hume Brophy in Europe and sold to Shamrock in 2025 with reportedly half of its $100M+ revenue from AI and data; FGS fused US public affairs with UK and German corporate affairs and reached a $1.7B enterprise value with KKR. The AI agents we would deploy first are a narrative early-warning monitor, a compliance-gated drafting agent and a synthetic-audience tester; each is backed by vendor evidence such as 85% faster review cycles (Writer) and a 0.90 survey correlation in one day (Aaru for EY), which we treat as upper bounds. Talent is the moat; the senior bench of LaBolt, Gibbs, Alexander and Whiting, partner equity on the FGS model, founder-to-practice-leader paths for acquired firms, and compensation held under 60% of net revenue are what keep the people the revenue walks out with. Our assumption-based roadmap takes revenue from about $105M to about $160M and EBITDA from about $22M to about $38M over 36 months, with headcount from about 400 to about 560 and recurring revenue at about 55%. At the 10-13x sponsor-exit range we estimate (PPHC trades at about 8.4x as the public floor), that implies roughly $384-499M of enterprise value after the 2028 cycle; that is an analyst scenario to pressure-test, not a forecast.

items.event: BSP makes a strategic anchor investment in Smith + Howard
items.lesson_for_bpi: A founder-led regional professional-services firm with a strong brand is the base; BPI (200+ staff, Apr 2023) started about twice as large.
First add-on lands in under a year and in an adjacent metro. BPI did the same with BOLDT (Dec 2023, 7.5 months after entry).
A specialist shop bought for capability, not geography. The BPI equivalents are Message House (message testing) and Agado (sports).

items.event: Acquires VIP Search / VIP Solutions (talent and staffing advisory)
items.lesson_for_bpi: Adjacent services raise wallet share per client. For BPI that means litigation and oversight communications (Mar 2026) and insights.

items.event: Signs agreement to acquire Fahrenheit Advisors
items.lesson_for_bpi: The regional-to-multi-state step. BPI's version is transatlantic: London became the #2 hub (Nov 2024).
Back-to-back closes six weeks apart show an integration machine. BPI's cadence peaked at Propper Daley (Mar 2025) followed by Agado (May 2025).
Density in the home region keeps going even after the firm goes national.
Later add-ons buy higher-margin advisory capability.
The last add-on before the sale is a tech-enabled specialty that sharpens the growth story. BPI's analogue would be a narrative-intelligence or data shop.

items.event: TPG signs definitive agreement to invest via TPG Growth
items.lesson_for_bpi: The exit buyer is a larger growth sponsor that pays for a scaled, multi-office portfolio company.

items.event: BSP completes sale of Smith + Howard to TPG (first exit)
items.location: 11 locations across the Southeast US and India
items.lesson_for_bpi: The full arc: 8x people, about 4x revenue, 9 add-ons in about 3.7 years (about 2.42 per year). BPI has done 6 add-ons in about 3 years (about 1.99 per year).

items.event: Falfurrias acquires Ballast Research, the seed of Penta
items.metric: first acquisition of the roll-up (data/research firm)
items.lesson_for_bpi: Same vertical, same DC base. The roll-up began with a research/data asset, not an agency.

items.event: Penta acquires Hume Brophy (global public affairs, ~100 professionals)
items.metric: ~100 professionals added; energy, transport, agribusiness, financial services
items.lesson_for_bpi: A European public-affairs add-on bought for its regulated-sector practices, the same play as BPI's BOLDT and 365 Sherpas.

items.event: Shamrock Capital acquires Penta from Falfurrias (terms undisclosed)
items.location: DC; NY; SF; London; Brussels; Paris; Dublin; Hong Kong
items.metric: reported $100M+ revenue, about half from proprietary AI/data/predictive analytics (Axios)
items.lesson_for_bpi: This is the closest exit comp for BPI's thesis. A data- and AI-heavy public-affairs portfolio company at about $100M revenue sold to a sector specialist sponsor about 5 years after the seed deal.

items.event: Finsbury, Glover Park and Hering Schuppener merge (Finsbury Glover Hering)
items.lesson_for_bpi: The transatlantic strategic-comms model: US public affairs plus UK financial PR plus German corporate affairs. BPI is assembling the same triangle (DC, London, Berlin).

items.event: Adds Sard Verbinnen, rebrands FGS Global
items.lesson_for_bpi: Scale plus a premium brand. Valued at $917M (Oct 2021).

items.event: WPP sells its ~50% stake to KKR at a $1.7B enterprise value
items.lesson_for_bpi: This is the ceiling valuation for scaled strategic comms. KKR then funded add-ons with a DDTL (rival-047).

items.event: CVC Fund VII partners with Teneo (replacing BC Partners)
items.metric: 800+ employees; headcount more than tripled and 9 acquisitions since 2015
items.lesson_for_bpi: The sponsor-to-sponsor pass in CEO advisory and comms: 9 acquisitions and 3x headcount in about 4 years earned a second-sponsor deal, reported at about $700M.
